customer-rep: Heads-up: AcmeCorp (Private VPC) is seeing intermittent 502s after last cert rotation. Only some clients fail — internal Java services fail with SSL errors, browsers are OK. Ticket #4521 attached.

alex: Thanks. Can you paste a sample client stacktrace and the VIP/hostname?

customer-rep: Stacktrace snippet: `javax.net.ssl.SSLHandshakeException: PKIX path building failed: unable to find valid certification path to requested target`. Host: acme-api.private.redwood:443. Failures reported from 2/5 DCs.

maya: Quick hypothesis: missing intermediate in the served chain OR OCSP stapling failing (and clients can't fetch AIA because of egress block). Can you run these from inside their VPC:```openssl s_client -showcerts -servername acme-api.private.redwood -connect acme-api.private.redwood:443```and```openssl s_client -connect acme-api.private.redwood:443 -status```and a `curl -v https://acme-api.private.redwood/health`

customer-rep: Ran the first openssl. Output shows leaf and root only (no intermediate). HAProxy cert bundle on proxy is `/etc/haproxy/certs/acme.pem` and points to rotator-managed secret.

nikhil: That matches a common rotor ordering issue: if the uploaded bundle has root before intermediate some TLS stacks will ignore the intermediate. Some clients (OpenSSL, modern browsers) will fetch AIA/issuer or build path differently and succeed; Java's default PKIX implementation often fails if intermediate isn't presented. In Private VPCs, AIA/OCSP fetches can be blocked by egress allowlists so those clients can't fetch the missing issuer.

alex: Can you check the rotator upload order + rotator logs? Look for log lines like: `rotator: wrote cert bundle (order: ...)`. Also `kubectl get secret rotator-acme -n rotator -o yaml` to inspect bundle.

customer-rep: Rotator log shows: `INFO rotator: uploaded cert bundle order=leaf,root,intermediate path=/bundles/acme.pem`. So intermediate ended up after root.

maya: OK that's the smoking gun — wrong bundle order. Workarounds: (1) customer uploads corrected bundle (leaf + intermediate + root, in that order) to the HAProxy/host, or (2) allow egress to issuer AIA/OCSP endpoints so clients can fetch issuer/staple. Immediate quick test: replace the bundle on one proxy and see if Java clients recover. Also run:```openssl verify -CAfile /etc/haproxy/certs/chain.pem leaf.pem``` to verify chain.

customer-rep: Ran `openssl s_client -status` — no OCSP response stapled. They cannot open egress to vendor issuer due to strict firewall. They requested a short-term mitigation they can apply without changing firewall rules.

tim: Short-term mitigation: upload corrected bundle (leaf + intermediate + root) to proxy secret (we can provide the bundle and steps) OR temporarily disable OCSP stapling on that proxy to let clients fall back (not ideal). Long-term: we will patch rotator to enforce canonical ordering and add a chain verification preflight. I'll open a PR and schedule a hotfix deploy.

alex: Action items: 1) Support to send step-by-step bundle replace instructions to customer and attach a prebuilt intermediate (we'll redact private keys). 2) SRE (tim/maya) to roll rotator fix + add preflight check (tim to owner). 3) Ask customer to open egress for AIA/OCSP endpoints if possible. I'll update ticket #4521 and set a 4-hour ETA for the rotator hotfix. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Ticket #4521 updated: owner=alex, severity=high, eta=4h.
